messages.text: The key surface is in `OnboardingStore.canContinue(.stats)` and the reset path from `MainTabView`. I’ve found the vitals screen is driven by a computed validation flag, so next I’m reading the actual validation and recent commits around the onboarding/profile model.

content.text: The key surface is in `OnboardingStore.canContinue(.stats)` and the reset path from `MainTabView`. I’ve found the vitals screen is driven by a computed validation flag, so next I’m reading the actual validation and recent commits around the onboarding/profile model.

messages.text: I found a concrete mismatch in the screenshot: height is metric, but weight is currently set to `Imperial`, so `65` is being validated as 65 lb. The store’s validation rejects imperial weight below 66 lb, which is why the button is disabled even though the fields look filled; now I’m checking whether this came from a recent reset/default/unit implementation gap and adding guardrails so it can’t silently trap you again.

messages.text: The Phase 1 onboarding commit introduced unit-specific ranges but no field-level reason for a disabled CTA. So the state in your screenshot is valid-looking to a human but invalid to the model: `weightUnit == .imperial` and `weight == 65`, just under the 66 lb minimum. I’m going to make unit switches convert the existing value instead of reinterpreting it, and surface the exact validation message on the vitals page.

messages.text:
Fixed. The blocker was not the reset itself: in your screenshot, **Weight** is set to **Imperial**, so `65` was being validated as **65 lb**. The onboarding validator required imperial weight to be `66...550`, so `canContinue(.stats)` stayed false. The Phase 1 onboarding work added that hidden unit-specific range check, but the UI gave no reason and did not convert values when units changed.

I fixed it in [OnboardingStore.swift](</Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/VirtualTrainer - mediapipe/VirtualTrainer/Models/OnboardingStore.swift:77>) and [OnboardingViews.swift](</Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/VirtualTrainer - mediapipe/VirtualTrainer/UI/OnboardingViews.swift:167>):
- Vitals now show exact validation messages, e.g. “Weight must be between 66 and 550 lb.”
- Switching units now converts the current value instead of reinterpreting it, so `65 kg` becomes `143.3 lb`.
- Added tests for the exact stuck state and the conversion path in [OnboardingModelTests.swift](</Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/VirtualTrainer - mediapipe/VirtualTrainerTests/OnboardingModelTests.swift:13>).

Verified with:
`xcodebuild test -workspace VirtualTrainer.xcworkspace -scheme VirtualTrainer -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17,OS=26.2'`

Full suite passed. The fix is committed as `1d1226e Onboarding fixes`.

::git-commit{cwd="/Users/satvik.bansal/Desktop/VirtualTrainer - mediapipe"}
